script.base: Hypothesis before pricing: BAL establishes control through Derrick Henry's lead rushing role, while TEN increasingly relies on passing to stay competitive. That gives Elic Ayomanor a plausible receiving opportunity without requiring Justice Hill to become a meaningful receiving option; halftime score, pace and garbage-time likelihood cannot be established from this pack.
script.flip1: TEN keeps the game close or leads, leaving BAL passing more than the base case assumes. Ayomanor's opportunity could shrink if TEN emphasizes rushing, while Hill's receiving under becomes vulnerable if additional passing work reaches him.
script.flip2: BAL builds an early, substantial lead and both offenses become less productive through the air. Hill's receiving under benefits, but Ayomanor's over becomes script-dependent if TEN's extra attempts do not produce usable targets.

pre_mortem: Ayomanor: It is Monday and the over lost because TEN's catch-up passing never reached its fourth-ranked target by supplied volume. Tate, Robinson and Helm absorbed the work, or TEN sustained rushing possessions instead; nine targets across three games is not a secure weekly floor. Hill: The under lost because a small yardage threshold required only one useful reception, or BAL needed more passing and Hill gained receiving work. His 22 receiving yards across three games do not reveal whether those yards were concentrated in one outing. Missing route and injury information prevents either counter-case from being dismissed, so both remain leans.
